extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent agents, and filing staff using the Indian Patent Office
extracted.subtask_short: drafting and filing Indian patent applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and procedural rules for preparing, filing, and processing patent applications (provisional and complete), specifications, drawings, abstracts, claims, fees, publication and related procedural matters before the Indian Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods of tendering and filing documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application, notice or other document may be tendered by hand, by post/registered post/speed post/courier service, or by electronic transmission duly authenticated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sent by post/courier/electronic transmission it is deemed filed at the time the mail would have been delivered in the ordinary course; proof of proper addressing and transmission is sufficient. Documents sent by post/courier are treated according to ordinary delivery times; in case of postal/courier delay the Controller follows the deemed date rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Addressing and modes of communication to parties
rubrics_metrics.description: Written communications to patentees, applicants or opponents at the address shown on the register or application/notice are deemed properly addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All notices and written communications (except special messenger) should be sent by registered post/speed post/courier or authenticated electronic transmission. Date of a notice is date of dispatch by those modes (unless Act/rules specify otherwise).

rubrics_metrics.name: Condonation of delay for parties receiving Office communications
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party is delayed in transmitting or resubmitting a document because of delay in receipt of a document from the Patent Office, the Controller may condone the delay on petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition must be made immediately after receipt, include a statement of circumstances and supporting evidence; the condoned delay cannot exceed the period between the date when the party should have received the communication and the actual date of receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document receipt counters and timings
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications and documents with fees and without fees are received at separate counters: Fee Counter (FC) and Non-Fee Counter (NFC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both counters close at 5 pm; documents by post/courier received at a separate counter; fee-counter staff generate Cash Book Receipts (CBRs) and stamp documents with CBR number, date, amount, application/patent numbers; documents are sent hourly to EDP for digitization; non-digitized docs sent daily to concerned sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language and paper format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: All documents must be written or typewritten or printed in Hindi or English, in large legible characters, deep indelible ink, on one side only of strong white A4 paper with specified margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Margins: at least 4 cm top and left, 3 cm bottom and right. Prefer line spacing 1.5 or double in non-script fonts (Arial, Times Roman, Courier), preferably font size 12.

rubrics_metrics.name: Signature transcription requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any signature not legible or written in a script other than Hindi or English must be accompanied by a transcription of the name in Hindi or English block letters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sequence listing submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Sequence listings of nucleotides and/or amino acids must be filed in electronic form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee equivalent to the corresponding number of pages must be paid for the sequence listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee payment modes and timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Fees can be paid in cash, electronic means, bank draft, or cheque payable to Controller of Patents drawn on a scheduled bank at the office location.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If draft/cheque is sent by post, fee is deemed paid on the date the instrument would have reached the Controller in ordinary course. The entire fee must accompany the document relevant to the fee; the Controller will not perform an act until fee is paid; fee once paid is not refundable. Prescribed fees are in the First Schedule. On transfer from a natural person to a non-natural person, any difference in fees must be paid by the new applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial processing and bibliographic handling
rubrics_metrics.description: On receipt the Office accords a date and serial number, digitizes, verifies, screens, classifies, uploads documents, arranges them in a file wrapper and prepares a bibliographic sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Application is screened for International Patent Classification, technical field allocation, relevance to defence/atomic energy, and for correcting/completing the abstract. Requests for examination get separate serial numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scrutiny checklist for applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Office checks jurisdiction, proof of right to file, prescribed formats and completeness of filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific checks include: correct jurisdiction; proof of right filed (or within six months or via petition); documents in prescribed forms (requests, petitions, assignment deeds, translations); correct paper size, font, spacing; signatures; abstract and drawings format; meaningful claims present; Power of Attorney or attested copy; Form-5 where applicable; Form-6 if invention assigned; if right assigned to legal entity, balance fees invited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy directions for defence-related inventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Controller may issue secrecy directions if invention pertains to subject matter relevant to defence, prohibiting publication and referring to Central Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Central Government considers the direction, reviews every six months; applicant can request reconsideration; directions under Section 35 prevent the Controller from deciding on grant/refusal while in force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Atomic energy inventions restriction and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: No patent is granted for inventions relating to atomic energy under the Atomic Energy Act; prior permission is required for filing abroad for such inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application falls under Atomic Energy Act, Controller refers it to Central Government which may issue binding directions; applicant must obtain prior permission before making applications or communications abroad unless six weeks have passed without reply to a permission request; Central Government opinion is not appealable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Withdrawal of application and effect on publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may withdraw application in writing and by paying prescribed fee at any time before grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawn within 15 months from filing or priority date the application will not be published; it is desirable to state withdrawal under Section 11A(3)(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard publication timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications are not public before expiry of 18 months from filing or priority; at the end of 18 months the Application is published unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: secrecy direction in force; application abandoned under s.9(1); withdrawn three months prior to publication (i.e., before end of 15th month). Patent Office publishes in Official e-Journal ordinarily within one month after 18 months. No application published unless power of authority (if applicable) filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early publication procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may request early publication by filing Form-9 with prescribed fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fee: Rs.2,500 for natural person(s) or Rs.10,000 for a legal entity other than natural person(s). Early publication not granted for defence/atomic energy subject matter. If request accepted, application published within one month of request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required particulars in Official Patent Journal publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Journal is published weekly with specific particulars about each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particulars include: application number; date of filing; title of invention; publication date; International Patent Classification; name and address of applicant; name of inventor(s); priority details; references to patent of addition/divisional and parent filing date; abstract; number of claims; drawings (if any).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of publication
rubrics_metrics.description: After publication the Specification and drawings are made available to the public; biological materials deposited become available; patentee can claim damages from date of publication but can sue only after grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depository institution will make biological material available after publication; certain pre-2005 applications have rights accruing from date of grant with limited remedies; no patent shall be granted before expiry of six months from publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A complete specification must fully and particularly describe the invention so that a person skilled in the art may perform it, and must disclose the best method known to the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specification is a techno-legal document; mandatory to disclose all features; may be provisional or complete; must be submitted in Form-2 with Form-1 in duplicate and prescribed fee. First page must contain title, name/address/nationality of applicants and preamble to the description. Drawings where required. Controller may require models/samples before grant (which do not form part of specification).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional specification purpose and effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional specification is a written disclosure when invention is presentable but not final; it secures a priority date and is accorded a filing date and application number on receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A provisional must be followed by a complete specification within 12 months or it is deemed abandoned (though post-dating option exists within 12 months in some cases). Two cognate provisionals may be covered by a single complete specification filed within 12 months from first provisional. Complete specification can be converted to provisional within 12 months in some cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional specification content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A provisional specification must contain the title and description and start with the preamble 'The following Specification describes the invention.' Claims may not be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Description should include field of invention, background, object and statement of the invention; include as much information as available to adequately distinguish from prior art. Provisional specification cannot be filed for Divisional, Convention or PCT National Phase Applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete specification essential elements
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete specification must (1) fully and particularly describe the invention and operation/use and method of performing it, (2) disclose the best method known, (3) end with claim(s) defining the scope of protection, and (4) reference deposit of biological material if applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are statutory requirements under Section 10; failure to meet them can affect patentability and validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Title drafting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Title should be sufficiently indicative of inventive features, brief, precise, free from fancy expressions or ambiguity, normally consisting of around fifteen words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include inventor's name, the word 'Patent', words in other languages, abbreviations like 'etc' or fancy brand-like expressions. Title need not match preamble of main claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Field of invention and use statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Description should preferably begin with a general statement indicating the subject matter (e.g., 'This invention relates to…') and may state advantages and industrial applicability.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant may substantiate industrial applicability in this section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior art disclosure and problem to be solved
rubrics_metrics.description: Description should indicate the status of technology in the field with reference to developments, patents and pending applications; when an improvement, the closest prior art should be stated and distinguished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The description must fully and particularly describe the invention while clearly distinguishing it from the closest prior art known to the applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Objects of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects section should clearly bring out the necessity of the invention, the technical problems with existing technology and the solution provided by the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State objects with phrases such as 'The principal object of this invention is …', 'Another object …', etc., to make the solution and differences clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of the invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a summary before detailed description that sets forth the distinguishing novel features of the invention for which protection is desired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary declares different aspects of the invention and should make the novel features clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detailed description sufficiency and examples
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed description must be furnished in sufficient detail to give a complete picture, enabling a skilled person to perform the invention without further experimentation; include examples/drawings as needed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe nature of improvements/modifications vs prior art; include sufficient examples (especially for chemical inventions); reference drawings specifically; avoid vague slang/colloquialisms. For biological material not publicly available, deposit with International Depository Authority (e.g., MTCC) on/before filing date and reference deposit within three months; disclose source and geographical origin of biological material; sequence listings for biotech inventions must include relevant numbers and be given in electronic form with corresponding fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drawings requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Drawings or sketches should be on separate sheets, neat and clear on durable paper, A4 size with specified margins.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drawings should be on a scale large enough to show invention; dimensions should not be marked; sheets must be numbered sequentially and bear applicant name (left top), sheet numbering (right top) and applicant or agent signature (right bottom). No descriptive matter on drawings except flow diagrams.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract drafting rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Every complete specification must be accompanied by an abstract providing concise technical information enabling a searcher to assess whether to consult the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Abstract should start with title, indicate technical field, technical problem, solution and principal uses; may include chemical formula if necessary; limit 150 words; indicate drawing figure numbers if drawings accompany abstract; Controller may amend the abstract for clarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best method disclosure requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Complete specification must describe the best method of performing the invention known to the applicant, including that acquired during the provisional protection period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims as defining legal scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims state technical facts in legal terms defining the scope of invention sought; no monopoly is obtained for matter not claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims are critical and should be drafted carefully to cover aspects distinguishing from prior art; what is not claimed is open to public use; claims form the protective boundary and should be clear and precise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity and clarity of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must relate to a single invention or to a group of inventions linked as a single inventive concept; claims shall be clear, succinct and fairly based on matter disclosed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim must be fairly supported by the description; lack of unity or clarity can lead to objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance and independence of individual claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Each claim is evaluated on its own merits; an objection to one claim does not invalidate others; applicants should claim all aspects to maximize protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should be concise, precise and accurate so others can identify boundaries; draft multiple claims covering different aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate breadth of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must not be too broad (to avoid covering public domain/others' subject matter) nor too narrow (which would reduce enforceability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with broad claims and progress to narrower dependent claims; avoid vague expressions like 'any novel matter' or subjective terms without definite values; many claims with differing scopes are useful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and structure of claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must follow the prescribed format: start with 'I/We claim', be serially numbered, start on a fresh page after description, be single-sentence, clear and not verbose; there is no limit on number but fees apply beyond ten.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim must be fairly based on disclosed matter and use terms found in or clearly inferred from the description. Avoid vague words ('thin', 'strong', 'any'). Trademarks should not be used unless unavoidable; if used, indicate registration status. A claim usually has preamble, transitional phrase (comprising, including, consisting of, consisting essentially of) and body. For improvements, use 'characterized by' or 'wherein' to separate prior art portion from novel features. The first claim is normally independent and should define essential novel features of preferred embodiment; multiple independent claims allowed if they fall under a single inventive concept.
